name: Textron Inc.
moat_justification: Leading Cessna/Beechcraft general-aviation franchise with installed-base aftermarket and Bell's MV-75/FLRAA program of record, but measured returns are middling (roic_proxy null in fundamentals.json, net margin ~6% TTM, gross margin under 18% where tagged), with government program concentration and cyclical jet demand.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 5.7%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.0%) vs bull-case tier C (10.8%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid aerospace/defense franchise, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $75.93 (weighted IRR 9.1%, IV@15 $38.89); it would need a price at or below $38.89 to clear the hurdle.
moat_for: Cessna and Beechcraft leading general-aviation brands with large installed base driving recurring aftermarket; Aviation backlog $8.0B
Bell MV-75 (FLRAA) program of record with multi-decade visibility plus H-1/V-22 sustainment; ITAR and qualification barriers
Diversified defense backlog (Bell $7.5B, Systems $3.3B) and qualification switching barriers
moat_against: Middling measured returns: roic_proxy unavailable, net margin ~6% TTM, gross margin under 18% where tagged; no proven pricing power through a cycle
US government program concentration: MV-75 funding gap puts $0.20-0.30 guided EPS and $150-250M cash flow at risk
Business-jet competition (Gulfstream, Embraer, Dassault, Bombardier) and cyclical demand
Q2 2026 execution drag: revenue +3% but segment profit flat, Aviation and Bell margins down; Industrial/EV transition and separation overhang
